blocker.summary: FINAL ROOT CAUSE FOUND, closing the entire r399-r451 investigation chain end to end. r451 re-armed the hardware watchpoint from r450 and let it run through to the known crash: confirmed definitively there is no second writer to the poisoned pool anywhere in the observed execution. Searching tools/materialize_native_import_stubs.py (already consulted in r448) found the missing-producer problem was already named by an earlier campaign cycle (r276, long before r399): sub_821CC008 derives a shared read-buffer size from queried file sizes, and a zero-fill in an earlier NtQueryInformationFile stub (r240) collapsed every size to 0, giving the queue buffer a 0-byte allocation -- exactly matching queue+332=0 seen live in r448's NtReadFile trace, today. A fix already exists (NtQueryInformationFile now calls native_guest_media_service().file_size() to report real sizes) but it cannot help for a file the media service never finds. Checked: build/ntsc-uj/source/assets/ contains ONLY default.xex. The actual content files (DATA00.PAC, DATA01.PAC, DATA.TBL, and other packages) exist in this workspace's own game-files/ directory (and both full retail ISOs in disc-image/) but tools/prepare.py (line ~400-402) only ever copies the XEX into source/assets/ -- nothing else is staged. This is the true root cause: not a codegen bug, not a missing native stub logic, but an incomplete asset-staging step that never mounts the game's real content packages for the native build. Full 10-step causal chain, every link now measured: prepare.py stages only the XEX -> native_guest_media_service() can't find DATA00.PAC -> NtQueryInformationFile's real-size fix has nothing to report -> sub_821CC008 derives a zero buffer size -> the allocated pool stays poisoned at 0xFE (r450) -> sub_821CC508 reads a 0xFE index byte (r449) -> computes an invalid handle, calls NtReadFile with garbage arguments (r448) -> the stub correctly refuses to fake success -> sub_821CC508 exhausts 5 retries (r446) -> sub_821D5F48 fails one of its 4 checks (r443), never constructs the renderer object at 0x82935D98 (r436-r441) -> sub_821D7DE0 logs non-fatally and proceeds anyway (r442) -> sub_821D6C20 dereferences the null object unguarded -> SIGSEGV (r435-r436). Not yet done: verify the exact path/format native_guest_media_service() expects for DATA00.PAC, then extend prepare.py to stage the real content files from game-files/, rebuild, and confirm the crash actually disappears. Named for r452 for exactly that -- deliberately not attempted this cycle, since it's a real source/build change that deserves its own rebuild-and-verify cycle rather than a rushed end-of-cycle edit. The native_vulkan_backend.cpp backlog commit decision (r433/r434/r438) remains the other open, user-dependent thread.
